open_points.subject: A20 Required tests item 2
open_points.text: A release whose list misses a package the instance would import, the Python version or the base image, or names any of them without an exact version or a digest, is not made.
open_points.question: Does “a package the instance would import” mean a package imported on the verification path, every package reachable on any supported runtime path, or the complete declared direct-and-transitive dependency closure?
options: Only packages imported while the release is verified
Every package that any supported runtime history may import
Every package in the declared direct-and-transitive dependency closure, whether or not a runtime path imports it
open_points.default_guess: Require the complete declared direct-and-transitive dependency closure and reject the release if any member is missing.

witness.initial: The program imports package X only when a caller uses an optional supported operation; ordinary startup and the release checks do not execute that operation.
events: The release process verifies a list that omits X without exercising the optional operation.
A caller invokes the optional operation.
outcomes: The release is not made because X is a package the instance would import on a supported path.
The release is made because the verification history never imported X; the later operation then cannot load it.
witness.observer: The release operator and the caller of the optional operation

open_points.subject: A20 Required tests item 2
open_points.text: or names any of them without an exact version or a digest
open_points.question: Does “any of them” cover every package named in the release list, including a package the instance would never import, or only the previously mentioned packages that the instance would import?
options: Every package named in the release list must have an exact version and digest
Only named packages the instance would import must have an exact version and digest
Packages the instance would never import are forbidden from the list
open_points.default_guess: Require an exact version and digest for every named package and reject entries that are not running dependencies.

witness.initial: A proposed release list names an installed diagnostics package that Registry never imports, and gives it neither an exact version nor a digest.
events: The release process checks the proposed list.
The installer would install every listed item if the release were made.
outcomes: The release is not made because “any of them” means any package the list names.
The release is made because the diagnostics package is not one of the packages the instance would import.

open_points.subject: A20 Python dependency verification
open_points.question: What concrete Python runtime artifact does the required digest identify and compare: a distribution archive, an executable, an installed runtime tree, or a constituent of the base image?
options: Digest a named Python distribution archive
Digest a canonical installed runtime tree
Treat Python as a constituent fixed only by the base-image digest
open_points.default_guess: Digest a named, immutable Python distribution artifact and require the installed runtime to be derived from that artifact.

witness.initial: The release names Python 3.13.1 and digest D; the downloaded Python archive has digest D, but the installed executable or runtime tree differs from the artifact expected by another verifier.
events: The installer compares the downloaded archive with D.
The installer prepares the runtime whose executable or installed tree has different bytes.
The release installation is evaluated against Required test 1.
outcomes: Installation succeeds because D denotes the distribution archive and that archive matches.
Installation fails and no instance starts because D denotes the executable or installed runtime tree and that value differs.
witness.observer: The release operator, who sees either a started instance or the required installation refusal

open_points.subject: A20 base-image identification
open_points.text: the base image of VM Platform's Registry environment by its digest
open_points.question: For the refusal in Required test 2, does an immutable base-image digest itself satisfy the requirement for an “exact version,” or must the release also name a separate exact image version or tag?
options: The digest is the base image's exact version and no tag is required
Both an exact version or immutable tag and a digest are required
Only the digest is required for the base image, despite the general wording about exact versions
open_points.default_guess: Treat the immutable image digest as the exact image identifier and require no mutable tag.

witness.initial: A proposed release names its base image only as registry.example/image@sha256:D, with no version tag.
events: The release process validates the dependency list under Required test 2.
outcomes: The release is made because the digest is an exact immutable image version.
The release is not made because the base image was named without a separate exact version.

open_points.subject: A20 release identity
open_points.text: the same release installed again gives the same list
open_points.question: What makes two installations installations of “the same release,” and may a release identifier ever be rebound to different contents?
options: A stable release label defines identity and may never be rebound
A content digest defines release identity, so changed contents are a new release even under the same label
A version plus a signed manifest digest defines release identity
open_points.default_guess: Identify a release by an immutable manifest digest and forbid rebinding any published release label to another digest.

witness.initial: A release is published under label R with dependency list L and is installed successfully.
events: The publisher later associates label R with different contents and dependency list L2.
An operator asks to install R again.
outcomes: The installation is refused because R denotes the same release and its dependencies changed from L to L2.
The installation is admitted as a new release because the changed contents define a new release despite reuse of label R.
witness.observer: The operator, who sees either refusal or a running instance with dependency list L2
